operations.evidence: The fire and rescue incident statistics release was published on 22 July 2026 and applies to England.
Publication timing and national scope do not establish conditions at a specific parcel.
Fire and rescue services attended 641,227 incidents in the year ending March 2026.
An attended-incident total is an England aggregate and cannot be assigned to an address without local incident data.
The 641,227 incidents were 5.8% more than the previous year's 605,936 incidents.
Year-on-year change may reflect service demand, recording and operational changes as well as underlying hazards.
Fire and rescue services attended 170,597 fires, 19% more than the previous year's 143,049.
National fire volume is not a parcel-level probability of fire.
There were 254 fire-related fatalities in 239 fatal fires, compared with 280 fatalities in 255 fatal fires in the previous year.
Fatality counts are small, can fluctuate and may be revised after coroners' findings.
Fires accounted for 27% of incidents, fire false alarms 40%, and non-fire incidents 34% in the year ending March 2026.
Rounded shares may not sum exactly and describe service workload rather than local risk.
There were 66,383 primary fires, 7.3% more than the previous year but 9.7% fewer than 10 years earlier.
Primary-fire trends are aggregated across different locations, property types and severities.
Fire and rescue services attended 39,859 building fires, 3.1% more than the previous year.
Building-fire totals combine dwelling and other-building incidents and are not property-specific.
Building fires represented 6.2% of all incidents, 23% of all fires and 60% of primary fires.
These proportions describe the national incident mix and must not be converted into a parcel score.
Fire and rescue services attended 255,047 fire false alarms, 1.6% more than the previous year.
False-alarm attendance can be affected by alarm systems, reporting behaviour and service procedures.
There were 172,247 fire false alarms due to apparatus, 2.6% fewer than the previous year.
Apparatus-related false alarms do not indicate an actual fire at a parcel.
There were 77,181 good-intent fire false alarms, 13% more than the previous year.
Good-intent calls are based on a belief that a fire exists and are not confirmed fire events.
There were 5,619 malicious fire false alarms, 2.1% fewer than the previous year.
The national count does not locate calls or measure neighbourhood safety.
Fire and rescue services attended 215,583 non-fire incidents, the largest financial-year figure since consistent data became available.
Non-fire incidents cover diverse activities and must not be treated as a single hazard measure.
Collaboration incidents reached 75,060 and accounted for 35% of non-fire incidents in the year ending March 2026.
Collaboration activity is influenced by multi-agency practice and does not directly measure local danger.
Effecting entry or exit was the largest collaboration category, with 41,130 incidents, 3.1% more than the previous year.
This service activity does not identify the cause, severity or parcel-level risk of each incident.
